# Fat necrosis of the breast

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Obstetrics/gynecology > Breast disorders > Fat necrosis of the breast*

[Original Article Link](/library/gt0F13)

---

## Summary

<u>Fat necrosis</u> of the <u>breast</u> is a benign nonsuppurative inflammatory lesion affecting the <u>adipose tissue</u>. It accounts for < 3% of all <u>breast</u> lesions and is usually the result of trauma (including blunt injury, <u>surgery</u>, or radiation) to the <u>breast</u>. <u>Fat necrosis</u> of the <u>breast</u> manifests as an ill-defined nontender <u>breast mass</u>; local <u>skin</u> changes may also be present. Age-appropriate <u>breast</u> imaging is indicated in all patients with a <u>palpable breast mass</u>. On <u>mammography</u>, <u>fat necrosis</u> may appear as an <u>oil cyst</u>; on <u>ultrasound</u>, it may appear as a <u>breast mass</u> of variable <u>echogenicity</u>. Clinical and imaging features can resemble those of <u>breast cancer</u>. If there is any suspicion of <u>malignancy</u> or if imaging is inconclusive, image-guided <u>biopsy</u> is indicated. Treatment is not usually required, but surgical excision should be considered if <u>malignancy</u> cannot be excluded, or imaging and pathology findings are discordant.

---

## Etiology

* Often associated with <u>soft tissue</u> trauma [[3]](/library/nib7Ht)

* <u>Surgery</u> or radiation [[2]](/library/WS1PAT0)

---

## Clinical features

* Typically manifests as an ill-defined nontender <u>breast mass</u>

* Often periareolar in location; can also occur peripherally

* <u>Breast</u> <u>skin</u> <u>retraction</u>, <u>erythema</u>, and/or <u>ecchymosis</u>

---

## Diagnosis

Follow age-appropriate diagnostic workup for a <u>palpable breast mass</u>. The findings specific to <u>fat necrosis</u> of the <u>breast</u> are described here.




### Imaging findings [[2]](/library/WS1PAT0)[[4]](/library/1S12AT0)[[5]](/library/sWYt5L)




* <u>Breast ultrasound</u>: variable; may be solid or cystic and <u>anechoic</u> or <u>hyperechoic</u> [[5]](/library/sWYt5L)

* <u>Mammography</u> [[2]](/library/WS1PAT0)[[5]](/library/sWYt5L)

* Fluid-filled oil cyst

* Coarse rim calcifications

* Spiculated mass

* <u>MRI</u> <u>breast</u> with and without contrast (not routinely ordered) [[2]](/library/WS1PAT0)[[5]](/library/sWYt5L)

* Round or oval lesions with <u>hypointense</u> T1 signals when fat suppression is performed

* Irregular or spiculated mass





![Oil cyst](media/d2luut3opztefnr7024gpttq.jpg)

Oil cyst




### Image-guided <u>biopsy</u>




* Indication: clinical suspicion of <u>malignancy</u>   [[2]](/library/WS1PAT0)

* Findings [[5]](/library/sWYt5L)[[6]](/library/bu1Hpi0)

* <u>Foam cells</u> and <u>multinucleated giant cells</u>

* <u>Necrotic</u> fat cells

* <u>Hemosiderin</u> deposition and <u>chronic inflammation</u>





![Breast fat necrosis](media/htddzdfr3j03ti12fnbted5t.jpg)

Breast fat necrosis

![Fat necrosis of the breast](media/qdwyakp35w3op9pybamf4ifp.jpg)

Fat necrosis of the breast




> [!TIP]
> Imaging findings of <u>fat necrosis</u> (e.g., spiculated mass, calcifications) may resemble those of <u>breast cancer</u>. <u>Biopsy</u> is recommended if there is clinical suspicion of <u>malignancy</u>.

---

## Treatment

* <u>Expectant management</u> is usually sufficient.

* Appropriate surveillance for benign  or probably benign lesions  [[7]](/library/Qe1uAf0)

* Consider surgical excision if:

* <u>Malignancy</u> cannot be excluded

* Imaging and pathology findings are discordant
